title: The Tide of Sandpiper Point
premise: Marine biologist Coral Ravensworth has spent ten years exchanging letters with a stranger known only as 'Tide'—the one person who knows the truth about the night her brother drowned at Sandpiper Point. When her anonymous correspondent, lighthouse keeper's son Elias Marsh, moves into the cottage next door to restore the decommissioned light before it's demolished, Coral must decide whether to reveal herself or protect the carefully contained life she's built. As demolition day approaches and a storm threatens both the lighthouse and a nesting sea turtle colony, Coral finally speaks the sentence she has rehearsed for a decade: that she was on the rocks that night, and that Elias's father died trying to save her brother. Choosing truth over invisibility, they save the turtles, lose the lighthouse, and find in each other a belonging neither dared to want.
about_author: Wren Galloway is the pen name of a former tide-pool docent who spent five summers counting hatchlings on the Carolina coast before turning to fiction. They write love stories for people who believe feelings are best handled like sea glass: worn smooth, held carefully, and never quite given up.

chapters.title: Counting Instead of Feeling
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Opening on Sandpiper Point's nesting beach, Coral catalogs loggerhead nests with clinical precision, narrating her philosophy that the heart is a trainable muscle. A letter from 'Tide' arrives; we learn of the decade-long correspondence without learning its origin. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: The Cottage Next Door
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A moving truck appears at the derelict keeper's cottage beside her rental. The new neighbor, Elias Marsh, introduces himself with sand-dusted hands and an unsettling familiarity in his phrasing. Coral feels seen in a way that alarms her. Beat: first crack in containment.

chapters.title: Letters I Never Sent
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Unpacking, he rereads ten years of replies to 'C.R.' and rehearses his own confession—that he knows who she is. Flashback seeds: his father was keeper of the Point light until the drowning night. Beat: dread braided with longing.

chapters.title: Demolition Notice
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The county posts notice: the lighthouse comes down in six weeks for a seawall project. Elias fights it publicly; Coral, whose research depends on the undisturbed point, is caught between allies. Their first argument crackles. Beat: duty versus desire begins its tug-of-war.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought In
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. Storm debris washes up a rusted tin box—inside, a child's shoe and a faded photograph of two boys and a girl on the jetty. Neither admits recognizing it. Beat: the past surfaces literally, tightening the noose of secrets.

chapters.title: Nest Nineteen
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Elias shows up at dawn to help relocate a threatened nest, surprisingly competent. Working shoulder to shoulder, banter softens into intimacy; Coral catches herself laughing and hates how good it feels. Beat: attraction becomes undeniable.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He drafts and burns three versions of his confession letter. Interleaved: memory of his father's last run into the surf, and the boy who survived. He decides to tell Coral in person—but she cancels their dinner. Beat: courage deferred.

chapters.title: Salt and Small Talk
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A town meeting about the lighthouse turns personal when a councilwoman implies Coral's presence at the Point is 'part of the problem.' Elias defends her fiercely, too fiercely. Walking home, they nearly kiss; Coral retreats. Beat: fear masquerading as restraint.

chapters.title: Postmark: Ten Years Ago
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She rereads Tide's first letter—the one that reached her at grief counseling after her brother Danny drowned—and admits to herself Tide is the only witness to what really happened. She almost writes the truth back tonight. Beat: confession within reach, then folded away.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Log
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Restoring the cottage, he finds his father's final logbook page, water-stained: 'Two in the water. Going back for the second.' He realizes his father died saving Danny—and that Coral may have been the second swimmer. Beat: the story reassembles itself wrong, then right.

chapters.title: Midnight Hatch
chapters.summary: Dual POV. An emergency: nest nineteen boils early under predator threat. Coral and Elias spend the night guiding hatchlings to the sea by lantern light, hands brushing, exhaustion dissolving defenses. At sunrise she tells him a half-truth about why she came to Sandpiper Point. Beat: trust built on partial honesty.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They kiss in the boathouse during a squall. Immediately after, Elias pulls back, saying he can't do this 'with something between us.' Coral, certain he means the lighthouse fight, agrees to oppose the demolition compromise together. Beat: intimacy achieved and immediately complicated.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. They pitch a joint plan—turtle sanctuary easement instead of seawall—to the county. Publicly they're partners; privately Elias is dying to confess and terrified the truth will cost him Coral. His sister arrives unannounced, knowing everything. Beat: external stakes rise as internal ones stall.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Knows
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Elias's sister Maren corners Coral, probing about 'the letters,' convinced Coral is C.R. Coral denies it convincingly—too convincingly—and then lies awake hating herself. Maren leaves a warning: 'He's carried this alone long enough.' Beat: guilt sharpens into urgency.

chapters.title: Compromise and Collapse
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The county rejects the easement but offers a stay if the lighthouse proves structurally sound. Elias, climbing the tower to document it, takes a fall. Coral reaches him first, and holding his bloodied hand, she nearly says everything. Beat: mortality collapses all timelines.

chapters.title: Hospital Letters
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. While Elias recovers, Coral writes him a letter she doesn't sign—Tide's voice—slipping it under his door, telling the truth of the drowning night in full. Then she panics and tries to retrieve it. Too late: he's read it. Beat: the sentence finally spoken, in ink instead of air.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Point
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He finds Coral on the jetty where it happened. The decade spills out: his father's death, her survivor's guilt, why each hid behind anonymity. Anger first—'You let me grieve you twice'—then devastation, then a raw, unfinished forgiveness. Beat: climax of truth.

chapters.title: The Storm Surge
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The hurricane arrives early, threatening nest twenty-two and stranding volunteers. Coral and Elias work the rescue together as equals, past fully laid down between them. The lighthouse, ironically, shelters them through the worst of it. Beat: love proven in action, not words.

chapters.title: What Survives
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Aftermath: the storm's damage forces the county's hand—the seawall plan is scrapped, and the lighthouse wins reprieve as a storm shelter landmark. Surveying the battered beach, Coral realizes survival isn't the price she feared paying; hiding was. Beat: thematic resolution.

chapters.title: Saying It Out Loud
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. On the relit lantern room's gallery—his restoration complete—he asks Coral to say the rehearsed sentence aloud. She does: 'I was there, and I've been writing to you because you were the only one who stayed.' He answers with his own decade-old sentence. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Boil Season
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Weeks later, hatchling season peaks; the town turns out to help, Coral no longer counting turtles to avoid feeling but to celebrate them. She and Elias are quietly, openly together. A final letter between them—signed with real names—is read side by side. Beat: joy earned.

chapters.title: The Light at Sandpiper Point
chapters.summary: Dual POV closing scene. One year later: the lighthouse relit as a private beacon, the sanctuary established, Coral's research thriving. On the gallery at dusk, they watch hatchlings glitter toward the horizon. Last line lands on belonging: some tides you survive, and some you learn to ride home. Beat: peace, forward-looking.
